content: No amount of anxiety makes any difference to anything that is going to happen.
author: Alan Watts
sourceWork: The Book: On the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are (1966)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Human beings are never a finished product; we exist in perpetual transit between our basic instincts and our highest potential. The tension we feel inside is not a flaw—it is the very engine of self-evolution.

In Alan Watts's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Growing into a fuller version of yourself requires crossing uncertain territory with no safety net. You have to be willing to outgrow the comfort of familiar limitations to step into who you are capable of becoming.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
